Jordan / Ben —

Quick triage notes:
- Initial telemetry: p95 ~ stable, p99 up ~3.2x starting 07:49 PDT on the Stonegate tenant.
- CPU/GPU utilization on the ded pool for Stonegate increased by ~18% post-flip.
- Root suspect: Q8 path in runtime is activating a slower attention kernel for long-sequence interactions; this shows as increased per-token time for sequences >512 tokens.
- Quality: we see elevated perplexity and a small but visible rise in generation divergence metrics for Q8 vs baseline FP16 for this model family.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Rollback Stonegate to v3.1/FP16 (fastest immediate fix).
2) If rollback is delayed, apply per-request routing to keep hot sessions on the FP16 variant while others can stay on Q8.

I’ll attach a short trace map and CPU/GPU samples to the internal thread.

Irene Choi\Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime\Redwood Inference

We understand the customer impact and are prioritizing rollback. Quick status:
- I’ve opened an emergency rollback job for Stonegate at 09:05 PDT. Expected completion: 15-20 mins.
- During the rollback window we’ll keep a degraded routing policy so sessions are pinned to FP16 variants to avoid cold path slowdowns.
- I’m preparing a mutual action plan (attached) that includes crediting for impacted minutes and a follow-up technical review.

Please expect a follow-up once rollback completes. We’ll also surface suggested guardrails to prevent blanket flips on Q8 for customers with long-tail session patterns.

-Ben
